Parlour library lamps added at the end of parts/room-2.mjs build(g): two chain lanterns (31,8,45 and 39,8,48) and a standing lantern at (41,4,44). Real build.nbt is still dark: the shell's air fill locks the room, so all five writes are refused and the room reads 11 dark, 91 dim cells.
Scratch copies, not in the build: the designer's three standing lanterns plus the two chains plus (41,4,44) give min 8 with 0 dim and 0 dark on the bare room. The chains alone give min 4 and 64 dim. The furnished result is still unmeasured.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt, but the room part is not lit in it.
left: BLOCKED: mansion shell.mjs:27 fills the room interior with "air" and runParts locks every cell an earlier part wrote, air included. The five lamp writes (31,8,45 lantern; 31,9,45 iron_chain; 39,8,48 lantern; 39,9,48 iron_chain; 41,4,44 lantern) are refused, so build.nbt has no lamps in this room. Fix belongs to the shell or the library (leave interior cells unwritten, or let room parts place into air). Not touched.

The designer's furniture is not written: build(g) has only the lamps, and the LEGEND/Y4-Y6 layers call is not yet in the module. The light numbers above assume the designer's standing lanterns at (29,4,45), (30,6,46) and (38,4,47), plus the candle at (38,6,46). Once the designer's layers land, rerun `mcd room --only "parlour library"` and confirm min >= 8 on the reading floor.
Current NEEDS WORK flags come from unbuilt furniture, not the lamps: the lantern at (30,6,46) floats until the west table slab (30,5,46) exists, and the walk reports (30,7,46) unreached.

No part builds a hearth yet (no hearth() call in any parts file; roofs.mjs only places chimneyStack), so the 'with the hearth lit' check cannot be run. Firebox light is not counted in any number above.

The bare-room measurements are a guide only; the designer asked for a check on the furnished room. The dim cells at (42,43) and (43,43) are bookshelf cells in the designer's Y4 layout, so they may not be floor after furniture lands. (43,44) is free and is the one dim floor cell the extra lantern lifts.

waste.what: Found out which lamp cells the shell had locked by trial: wrote lamps into build(g), ran make.sh, then read parts-report.json for refusals.
waste.cost: Two full make.sh runs plus reading the report; each lamp rejection showed up only after a whole rebuild.
waste.tool: mcd room (or the report) should list cells locked by an earlier part, with the part that locked them (here mansion shell, shell.mjs:27 air fill), before a write is attempted.

waste.what: Measured candidate lamp sets by hand: a scratch measure.mjs that loads build.nbt, adds lamp cells straight to a copy, and saves it; then one mcd room run per set (5 sets).
waste.cost: About 5 scratch nbt files and 5 room runs, plus reading each light map to find the dim cells.
waste.tool: A what-if flag on mcd room or mcd light (e.g. --lamps "hang,31,8,45 stand,41,4,44") that adds candidate lamps to an in-memory copy and reports the light map and the dim cells without going through runParts.

waste.what: Checked by grep whether any part builds the hearth, and cell by cell whether the designer's lamp spots were free air.
waste.cost: Several grep and node probes over parts/ and build.nbt.
waste.tool: mcd room should flag reserved or unbuilt features (P-hearth, planned furniture cells) for the room, so the check does not need a grep across parts.

companions.task: Write the furniture layers (Y4, Y5, Y6 via layers()) and the designer's three standing lanterns (29,4,45), (30,6,46), (38,4,47) and the lit candle (38,6,46), then confirm the reading floor reads min 8 with the real furniture in place.
Stop the shell's interior air fill (shell.mjs:27) from locking room air, or reserve the room cells for the room parts, so the lamps and furniture can be placed.
Cut the P-hearth firebox in the stack face toward the parlour, with the lit campfire, so the hearth light counts toward the reading floor.
